cards.note: Green, agricultural valleys with deforested hills to make way for farmland are most commonly seen in the north.
The Bay of Kotor has a touristy and populated feel to it, with many people dressed in swimwear. A distinct steep, rocky ridge can also be seen.
The Pljevlja Coal Mine can be recognized by the wide, artificial wall of gravel. The mine can often be seen from afar.
Dry mountains with a lack of trees are seen around Podgorica, and to the south of it. Vineyards are also commonly seen in this region.

Durmitor National Park can be recognized by a distinct landscape consisting of grassy, treeless mountains with a high-altitude feel.

The town of Žabljak is situated in this national park, and can be recognized by the landscape but also by the unique architecture.
A big part of the P4 road can be identified by the steep and rocky cliff sides.

Pine forests can be found in the north and a small area north of Nikšić and a small area south of Pljevlja, but most commonly in the east.

Tips to differentiate these areas: The north west has useally just normal hilly landscape. The north east is more mountainous than the north west. The small area north of Nikšić is very rocky and has alot of rocks along the road.
The Piva Lake is a famous and long lake that can be recognized by the blue water with big rocky cliffs around it.
Podgorica is the capital and largest city in Montenegro, and can be recognized by the modern buildings, wide roads and modern infrastructure.

This map shows the distribution of where rifts are found in gen 3 coverage. Although rifts are common in Montenegro, coastal rounds will almost never have them. By the coast, there will be a short antenna with no rifts. There will be a long antenna with rifts inland.

NOTE: An exception to this is the area around the coastal villages of Utjeha and Dobra Voda.
The Skadar Lake Bridge can be recognized by the railway and stone bollards next to the road.
Many small islands can be seen within Slansko Lake.
These distinct staircase-like mountainsides can be seen in the Cemi River Valley.

The southern part of the E80, between Orahovo and Đurmani, can be recognized by the yellow outer lines, wait, yellow outerlines? Yes, it has been overwritten by white outerlines, but you can still see a bit of yellow on the edge if you look closely.
